title: Coordinate covector dx^I exists as a continuous determinant covector
statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every map I : Fin n → Fin P (no monotonicity or injectivity assumed), there is an n-covector θ on ℝ^P with θ(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P. Here an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ, and Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). In words, θ(v) is the determinant of the n×n matrix whose (k, j) entry is the I(k)-th coordinate of v_j.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (I : Fin n → Fin P), ∃ θ : Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ v : Fin n → Euclid P, θ v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k))
